
# 1. Import data and codebook

The current code uses the synthetic dataset. Code developed here will be updated and rerun using the real registry data after the initial descriptive and quality-control review is complete.

```{r import-data}
# ============================================================
# FILE PATHS — UPDATE BEFORE RUNNING ON THE REAL DATA
# ============================================================

# ---- UPDATE PATH 1: DATASET ----
data_file <- "data/raw/synthetic_data.csv"

# ---- UPDATE PATH 2: MASTER CODEBOOK ----
codebook_file <- "Dissertation_Aim1_Master_Codebook.xlsx"


# ============================================================
# IMPORT DATA AND CODEBOOK — NO PATH CHANGES NEEDED BELOW HERE
# ============================================================

# Import dataset
dat <- read_csv(data_file)

# Import codebook sheets
region_codes  <- read_excel(codebook_file, sheet = "Region Codes")
comuna_codes  <- read_excel(codebook_file, sheet = "Comuna Codes")
closure_codes <- read_excel(codebook_file, sheet = "Closure Codes")
country_codes <- read_excel(codebook_file, sheet = "Country Codes")
```

# 2. Create date and calendar year variables

The variable `fecha_creacion_caso` contains the date of case creation as a character variable (for example, `10OCT2012`).

This section converts it to an R date and derives calendar year.

```{r create-date-year}
dat <- dat %>%
  mutate(
    fecha_creacion_date = parse_date(
      fecha_creacion_caso,
      format = "%d%b%Y",
      locale = locale("en")
    ),
    year = lubridate::year(fecha_creacion_date)
  )
```


# 3. Define analytic cohort

The planned Aim 1 study population includes individuals ages 15–65 with case creation dates from 2005–2023.

The final analytic cohort definition is still being determined. Three cohort definitions (A, B, and C) are being considered based on the selection of registry records and IPD confirmation/discard status.

The final cohort will contain one record per individual. The earliest qualifying record will be selected before applying the age and calendar-year restrictions.

For now, this section provides a preliminary record-level screening summary. No final cohort selection or restrictions are applied to `analytic_dat` yet.

## Preliminary sample flow

The table below shows the number of registry records meeting the age and calendar-year criteria. These counts are descriptive and do not represent the final person-level analytic cohort.

```{r sample-flow}
analytic_sample_flow <- tibble(
  Step = c(
    "Raw registry records",
    "Records with age 15-65 years",
    "Records with age 15-65 years and calendar year 2005-2023"
  ),
  N = c(
    nrow(dat),

    dat %>%
      filter(
        !is.na(edad_ano_creacion_caso),
        between(edad_ano_creacion_caso, 15, 65)
      ) %>%
      nrow(),

    dat %>%
      filter(
        !is.na(edad_ano_creacion_caso),
        between(edad_ano_creacion_caso, 15, 65),
        !is.na(year),
        between(year, 2005, 2023)
      ) %>%
      nrow()
  )
)

kable(
  analytic_sample_flow,
  caption = "Preliminary record-level screening"
)
```

## Create analytic dataset

The final analytic dataset will contain one record per individual, selected according to the chosen cohort definition.

The age (15–65 years) and calendar-year (2005–2023) restrictions will be applied after selecting the earliest qualifying record for each individual.

```{r create-analytic-dataset}
# Temporary placeholder for exploratory analyses.
# Currently contains all registry records.

analytic_dat <- dat

# TODO:

# 3. Apply age restriction: 15-65 years.
# 4. Apply calendar-year restriction: 2005-2023.
```

# 4. Create Aim 1 analysis variables

This section creates analysis variables while preserving the original registry variables.

Region, comuna, and country-of-origin codes are linked to their corresponding names using the master codebook. Original numeric codes are retained.

Categories are retained as they appear in the source data, and missing values are kept as NA. Categories may be collapsed later after reviewing their distributions in the real registry data.

```{r analysis-variables}
# Make sure codebook columns are numeric to match registry codes.
region_codes <- region_codes %>%
  mutate(`Region Code` = as.numeric(`Region Code`))

comuna_codes <- comuna_codes %>%
  mutate(`Comuna Code` = as.numeric(`Comuna Code`))

country_codes <- country_codes %>%
  mutate(`Country Code` = as.numeric(`Country Code`))

# Check that codebook keys are unique before joining.
stopifnot(
  !anyDuplicated(region_codes$`Region Code`),
  !anyDuplicated(comuna_codes$`Comuna Code`),
  !anyDuplicated(country_codes$`Country Code`)
)

# Keep only the code and name columns needed for each join.
region_lookup <- region_codes %>%
  select(`Region Code`, `Region name`)

comuna_lookup <- comuna_codes %>%
  select(`Comuna Code`, `Comuna`)

country_lookup <- country_codes %>%
  select(`Country Code`, `Country Name`)

analytic_dat <- analytic_dat %>%

  # Add region names
  left_join(
    region_lookup,
    by = c("cmd_cod_deis_regi_benef" = "Region Code")
  ) %>%

  # Add comuna names
  left_join(
    comuna_lookup,
    by = c("comuna" = "Comuna Code")
  ) %>%

  # Add country-of-origin names
  left_join(
    country_lookup,
    by = c("cmd_cod_pais_origen" = "Country Code")
  ) %>%

  mutate(
    # Outcome
    age = edad_ano_creacion_caso,

    # Primary exposure
    calendar_year = year,

    # Individual characteristics
    sex = na_if(trimws(cmd_sexo_benef), ""),
    chilean_foreign = na_if(trimws(cmd_cond_chile_extranj), ""),
    fonasa_tramo = na_if(trimws(cmd_carga_tramo_benef), ""),

    country_origin = case_when(
      is.na(cmd_cod_pais_origen) ~ NA_character_,
      is.na(`Country Name`) ~ paste0(
        "Unmapped code: ", cmd_cod_pais_origen
      ),
      TRUE ~ as.character(`Country Name`)
    ),

    # Geographic characteristics
    region = case_when(
      is.na(cmd_cod_deis_regi_benef) ~ NA_character_,
      is.na(`Region name`) ~ paste0(
        "Unmapped code: ", cmd_cod_deis_regi_benef
      ),
      TRUE ~ as.character(`Region name`)
    ),

    comuna_name = case_when(
      is.na(comuna) ~ NA_character_,
      is.na(`Comuna`) ~ paste0(
        "Unmapped code: ", comuna
      ),
      TRUE ~ as.character(`Comuna`)
    ),

    # Clinical setting variables
    establishment_level = na_if(
      trimws(desc_nivel_estab_crea_caso), ""
    ),
    establishment_type = na_if(
      trimws(desc_tipo_estab_crea_caso), ""
    ),

    # Case status variables
    ipd_confirmed = na_if(trimws(ipd_cofirmado), ""),
    ipd_discarded = na_if(trimws(ipd_descartado), "")
  )
```



# 5. Descriptive characteristics of the analytic cohort

This section describes the overall characteristics of the analytic cohort, including age at case creation, individual characteristics, geographic characteristics, clinical setting, and IPD status.

All categories are retained as they appear in the source data. Missing values are included in the descriptive tables, and no categories are collapsed at this stage.

Results are preliminary until the final person-level analytic cohort is defined in Section 3.

## Overall sample size

```{r table1-n}
table1_n <- tibble(
  Measure = c(
    "Total records",
    "Unique individuals"
  ),
  N = c(
    nrow(analytic_dat),
    n_distinct(analytic_dat$id_persona, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
)

kable(
  table1_n,
  caption = "Dataset size"
)
```

## Age at case creation

```{r table1-age}
age_values <- analytic_dat$age
age_nonmissing <- age_values[!is.na(age_values)]

age_table <- tibble(
  Statistic = c(
    "N (non-missing)",
    "Mean (SD)",
    "Median",
    "Q1 (25th percentile)",
    "Q3 (75th percentile)",
    "IQR",
    "Minimum",
    "Maximum",
    "Missing"
  ),
  Value = c(
    length(age_nonmissing),
    if (length(age_nonmissing) > 1) {
      paste0(
        round(mean(age_nonmissing), 1),
        " (",
        round(sd(age_nonmissing), 1),
        ")"
      )
    } else {
      NA_character_
    },
    if (length(age_nonmissing) > 0) round(median(age_nonmissing), 1) else NA,
    if (length(age_nonmissing) > 0) round(as.numeric(quantile(age_nonmissing, 0.25)), 1) else NA,
    if (length(age_nonmissing) > 0) round(as.numeric(quantile(age_nonmissing, 0.75)), 1) else NA,
    if (length(age_nonmissing) > 0) round(IQR(age_nonmissing), 1) else NA,
    if (length(age_nonmissing) > 0) min(age_nonmissing) else NA,
    if (length(age_nonmissing) > 0) max(age_nonmissing) else NA,
    sum(is.na(age_values))
  )
)

kable(
  age_table,
  caption = "Age at case creation"
)
```

## Helper function for categorical characteristics

This function calculates the frequency and percentage for each category, including missing values. Percentages use the total number of observations as the denominator.

```{r table1-helper}
table1_cat <- function(data, variable, characteristic_name) {

  data %>%
    count({{ variable }}, name = "n") %>%
    mutate(
      Characteristic = characteristic_name,
      Category = if_else(
        is.na({{ variable }}),
        "Missing",
        as.character({{ variable }})
      ),
      Percent = round(100 * n / sum(n), 1)
    ) %>%
    select(Characteristic, Category, n, Percent)
}
```

## Individual characteristics

```{r table1-individual}
table1_individual <- bind_rows(
```

## Geographic characteristics

This section describes region, comuna, and country of origin using the original registry codes and their corresponding names from the master codebook.

All geographic categories are retained, including unknown, missing, and unmapped values.

### Region

```{r table1-region}
table1_region <- analytic_dat %>%
  count(
    cmd_cod_deis_regi_benef,
    region,
    name = "n"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    `Region code` = coalesce(
      as.character(cmd_cod_deis_regi_benef),
      "Missing"
    ),
    `Region name` = coalesce(region, "Missing"),
    Percent = round(100 * n / sum(n), 1)
  ) %>%
  select(
    `Region code`,
    `Region name`,
    n,
    Percent
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(n))

kable(

)
```

# 6. Descriptive temporal trends

This section examines changes in age at case creation across calendar years, overall and by selected individual and structural characteristics.

These analyses are descriptive. Categories are retained as they appear in the source data, and no statistical models are fitted in this section.

Results are preliminary until the final analytic cohort is defined.

## Age at case creation by calendar year

```{r age-by-year}
age_by_year <- analytic_dat %>%
  group_by(calendar_year) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    n_age = sum(!is.na(age)),
    mean_age = mean(age, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_age = sd(age, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_age = median(age, na.rm = TRUE),
    q1_age = as.numeric(quantile(age, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE)),
    q3_age = as.numeric(quantile(age, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE)),
    iqr_age = IQR(age, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(calendar_year)

kable(
  age_by_year,
  digits = 1,
  col.names = c(
    "Calendar year",
    "n",
    "N with age",
    "Mean age",
    "SD",
    "Median age",
    "Q1",
    "Q3",
    "IQR"
  ),
  caption = "Age at case creation by calendar year"
)
```

## Overall mean age trend

```{r mean-age-trend}
ggplot(
  age_by_year,
  aes(
    x = calendar_year,
    y = mean_age
  )
) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq(2005, 2023, by = 2)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Mean Age at Case Creation by Calendar Year",
    x = "Calendar year",
    y = "Mean age at case creation"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Overall median age trend

```{r median-age-trend}
ggplot(
  age_by_year,
  aes(
    x = calendar_year,
    y = median_age
  )
) +

  ) +

    x = "Calendar year",
    y = "Median age at case creation"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Helper function for subgroup trends

This function summarizes age at case creation by calendar year and subgroup.

```{r trend-helper}
trend_by_group <- function(data, variable) {

  data %>%
    group_by(calendar_year, {{ variable }}) %>%
    summarise(
      n = n(),
      n_age = sum(!is.na(age)),
      mean_age = mean(age, na.rm = TRUE),
      sd_age = sd(age, na.rm = TRUE),
      median_age = median(age, na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    arrange(calendar_year, {{ variable }})
}
```

## Age by sex and calendar year

```{r age-trend-sex}

kable(
```

# 7. Aim 1 regression models

The planned Aim 1 regression analyses will evaluate temporal trends in age at case creation and examine whether these trends differ across individual and structural characteristics.

Linear regression models will be used to estimate mean differences in age at case creation. Model specifications will be finalized after the analytic cohort and variable categories are established.

## Model 1: Unadjusted temporal trend

This model will estimate the unadjusted annual change in mean age at case creation.

Outcome: Age at case creation

Exposure: Calendar year
